title: Fix mobile app stuck on loading/skeleton after Version 18

requirements.text: Prevent the app from staying indefinitely in the loading/skeleton UI on mobile by ensuring actor initialization failures and long-running actor initialization are surfaced to the UI as an error state (instead of keeping `isFetching/isLoading` true forever).

quotes: App is not loading correctly (see attached). Can you make it so that it loads correctly?

acceptanceCriteria: When loading the app on mobile and the backend/agent/actor initialization fails, the UI exits the skeleton state and shows an error banner/message within a bounded time (e.g., <= 15 seconds) rather than displaying the skeleton indefinitely.
If actor initialization succeeds, the skeleton transitions to the authenticated view and monthly totals/habit grid rendering without requiring a manual refresh.

requirements.text: Add a user-visible recovery path when loading fails: provide a clear error UI (English text) with a primary action to retry loading (refetch/recreate actor + refetch habits) without requiring the user to close the tab.

quotes: App is not loading correctly (see attached). Can you make it so that it loads correctly?

acceptanceCriteria: When a loading error occurs, the screen shows an error message (not a skeleton) and a Retry button.
Tapping Retry triggers a new attempt to initialize the actor (if needed) and refetch habits, and the UI reflects success or failure accordingly.

requirements.text: Harden actor initialization so it cannot hang indefinitely: wrap actor creation and `_initializeAccessControlWithSecret(...)` in a timeout and propagate timeout/initialization errors through `useActor()` so `useHabits()`/`BecomingView` can render an error instead of remaining stuck in a loading state.

quotes: App is not loading correctly (see attached). Can you make it so that it loads correctly?
Happened on mobile but not sure

acceptanceCriteria: If `_initializeAccessControlWithSecret` or actor creation does not complete within the timeout window, the frontend receives a deterministic error state and stops showing the skeleton.
No backend state migration is required to implement this change.

requirements.text: Adjust the loading-state logic in the main view so that it does not rely on a condition that can remain true indefinitely (e.g., `isInitializing`/actor fetching) and so that error states take precedence over skeleton rendering for authenticated users.
acceptanceCriteria: For an authenticated user, if the habits query cannot run because actor initialization errored, the error UI is shown (not the auth notice and not the skeleton).
For an authenticated user, the skeleton is only shown during an active, bounded loading attempt; afterward the UI resolves to either data or an error UI.

constraints: Do not edit files under `frontend/src/components/ui` (compose them instead).

Do not modify immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT (e.g., do not edit `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts` or `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts` directly if they are considered immutable in this environment; apply fixes by adding safe wrappers/adapters or adjusting calling code where allowed).
Keep Motoko logic in the single main actor (`backend/main.mo`); only add `backend/migration.mo` if an actual state upgrade is required.
nonGoals: Adding new product features beyond fixing the loading/skeleton issue and providing retry/error handling.
Changing authentication providers (Internet Identity remains the only auth mechanism).
